# `silk/time/relative`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Periods measured from a starting point: [`RelativeTo`](#RelativeTo) rounds a `Period`, gives its total in one
unit, and changes its largest unit.

## When to use

Use [`RelativeTo`](#RelativeTo) for a question about a `Period` whose answer depends on where the period
starts: how many months 100 days are, what `P1M45D` is in months and days, or what a period is
when rounded to whole weeks. Months and years have different lengths, and in a time zone a day
has 23 or 25 hours on the day of a change, so a period alone cannot answer.

To round an exact span, use `Duration.round`. To get the period between two dates, use the
`periodUntil` function of the date types.

## Details

A [`RelativeTo`](#RelativeTo) is a starting point: a `PlainDate`, where every day is 24 hours, or a
`ZonedDateTime`, where days have the length that they have in the zone. Each function moves
from the starting point by the whole period, as `addPeriod` does, and measures the way to the
point reached.

The functions follow `Temporal.Duration.prototype.round` and `total` of ECMAScript Temporal
with a `relativeTo` option.

## Examples

### Count, balance, and round a period from a date

```silk
import silk.core.option { Option }
import silk.time.period { DateUnit, Period }
import silk.time.plain_date { PlainDate }
import silk.time.relative { PeriodRounding, RelativeTo }
import silk.time.rounding { RoundingMode }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let start = RelativeTo.date(PlainDate.make(2027, 1, 1))
  // January has 31 days and February has 28, so 45 days are one and a half months.
  if let Option<f64>.Some { value: months } = start.total(Period.ofDays(45), DateUnit.Month) {
    if months != 1.5 {
      return 1
    }
  }
  if let Option<Period>.Some { value: balanced } = start.balance(Period.ofDays(45), DateUnit.Month) {
    if balanced.months() != 1 || balanced.days() != 14 {
      return 2
    }
  }
  let toMonths = PeriodRounding.toUnit(DateUnit.Month, RoundingMode.HalfExpand)
  if let Option<Period>.Some { value: rounded } = start.round(Period.ofDays(45), toMonths) {
    if rounded.months() != 2 || rounded.days() != 0 {
      return 3
    }
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `RelativeTo` with `import silk.time.relative { RelativeTo }`.

<a id="PeriodRounding"></a>

## `PeriodRounding`

```silk
pub struct PeriodRounding
```

How [`RelativeTo.round`](#RelativeTo.impl.round) rounds a period: the smallest unit or step that stays, the mode, and
the largest unit of the result.

### Details

[`PeriodRounding.toUnit`](#PeriodRounding.impl.toUnit) rounds to whole years, months, weeks, or days, and
[`PeriodRounding.toStep`](#PeriodRounding.impl.toStep) rounds the time part to a step such as 15 minutes.

Without [`PeriodRounding.upTo`](#PeriodRounding.impl.upTo) or [`PeriodRounding.asTime`](#PeriodRounding.impl.asTime), the largest unit of the result
is the largest unit of the period that is not zero, or the unit that the period is rounded
to when that is larger.

<a id="PeriodRounding.impl.toStep"></a>

### Associated function `toStep`

```silk
pub fn toStep(step: TimeIncrement, mode: RoundingMode) -> PeriodRounding
```

Returns the rounding of the time part to a multiple of `step`.

#### Details

A step of one day is the rounding to whole days, as with `toUnit(DateUnit.Day, mode)`.
`TimeIncrement.one(TimeUnit.Nanosecond)` rounds nothing, and is the way to change only the
largest unit.

<a id="PeriodRounding.impl.every"></a>

### Method `every`

```silk
pub fn every(self: Self, count: u32) -> PeriodRounding
```

Returns this rounding to a multiple of `count` units, such as every 3 months. It has an
effect only on a rounding from [`PeriodRounding.toUnit`](#PeriodRounding.impl.toUnit).

#### Gotchas

A `count` of 0 traps. With a count above 1, the result must have one unit: a rounding
whose largest unit is not the rounded unit has no result, because the larger units would
take parts of the multiple.

<a id="PeriodRounding.impl.upTo"></a>

### Method `upTo`

```silk
pub fn upTo(self: Self, largest: DateUnit) -> PeriodRounding
```

Returns this rounding with `largest` as the largest unit of the result.

#### Details

With `DateUnit.Month`, a result has months, days, and a time part, and no years or weeks.
A largest unit that is smaller than the unit of the rounding has no result.

<a id="PeriodRounding.impl.asTime"></a>

### Method `asTime`

```silk
pub fn asTime(self: Self) -> PeriodRounding
```

Returns this rounding with a result that has only a time part: the exact span of the
period from the starting point. It has no result with a rounding from
[`PeriodRounding.toUnit`](#PeriodRounding.impl.toUnit).

<a id="RelativeTo"></a>

## `RelativeTo`

```silk
pub struct RelativeTo<'z>
```

A starting point that periods are measured from.

### Details

[`RelativeTo.date`](#RelativeTo.impl.date) starts at midnight of a date and counts every day as 24 hours.
[`RelativeTo.zoned`](#RelativeTo.impl.zoned) starts at a `ZonedDateTime` and counts days on the calendar of its zone.

Every function has no result when a date that it needs is outside the range of the date
types.

<a id="RelativeTo.impl.span"></a>

### Method `span`

```silk
pub fn span(self: Self, period: Period) -> Option<Duration>
```

Returns the exact span from the starting point to the point that `period` reaches.

#### Details

From a date, one day is 24 hours. From a `ZonedDateTime`, the span of `P1D` is 23 or 25
hours over a daylight saving change.

<a id="RelativeTo.impl.total"></a>

### Method `total`

```silk
pub fn total(self: Self, period: Period, unit: DateUnit) -> Option<f64>
```

Returns `period` as a count of `unit`, with a fraction for the part of a unit.

#### Details

The whole units are counted on the calendar from the starting point, and the fraction is
the part of the next unit that the rest covers: from January 1, 45 days are 1 month and 14
of the 28 days of February, so 1.5 months. The result is negative for a negative period.

<a id="RelativeTo.impl.balance"></a>

### Method `balance`

```silk
pub fn balance(self: Self, period: Period, largest: DateUnit) -> Option<Period>
```

Returns the period from the starting point to the point that `period` reaches, with
`largest` as its largest unit.

#### Details

From January 1, `P45D` with `DateUnit.Month` is `P1M14D`, and `P1M14D` with `DateUnit.Day`
is `P45D`. A time part of 24 hours or more moves into the days.

<a id="RelativeTo.impl.round"></a>

### Method `round`

```silk
pub fn round(self: Self, period: Period, rounding: PeriodRounding) -> Option<Period>
```

Returns `period` rounded as `rounding` says.

#### Details

The period is first put in the units from the largest unit of the rounding down, as
[`RelativeTo.balance`](#RelativeTo.impl.balance) does. The rounded unit then takes one of the two values around the
period: for whole months, the result is the number of months before the point reached or
the next one, by the part of that month that the rest covers. A unit that reaches the
next larger unit moves into it: `P11M20D` rounded to months is `P1Y`.

`RoundingMode.HalfExpand` rounds to the nearest value, and away from zero from the middle.

#### Gotchas

There is no result when the largest unit of the rounding is smaller than its smallest
unit, or when [`PeriodRounding.every`](#PeriodRounding.impl.every) has a count above 1 and the largest unit is not the
rounded unit.
